idiom_name: discriminated-union event contract + typed emitter/EventTarget; runtime validator at the wire boundary
implementation_notes: The TypeScript event contract is a discriminated union: a literal type field on every member lets the compiler narrow with a switch and prove exhaustiveness with a never check, which replaces the event class hierarchy and the runtime type switch. Delivery reuses the JavaScript platform (EventTarget/CustomEvent, EventEmitter, or a small typed emitter wrapper); because types are erased, an event arriving from a broker is unknown until a schema validator (zod, valibot, io-ts) parses it into the union - that parse is the runtime replacement for the type discriminator and belongs at the boundary, so all downstream code can trust the narrowed type. Keep the literal tags in one exported type and derive handler maps from it.
pitfalls: Discrimination only works on literal types: widening the type field to string (or using an interface without literal tags) silently degrades to a non-discriminated union and narrows nothing.
JSON.parse returns any/unknown - the union's guarantee starts only after a runtime validator has accepted the value; validating in one boundary function avoids per-handler parsing.
Exhaustiveness checks catch a new member only where the switch is compiled, so keep the union in one shared package rather than per-service copies that drift.
Listener leaks and synchronous dispatch are inherited from the JS runtime: use { once: true }/AbortSignal and keep publish handlers short.
